verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection ... closes'; s6: 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB)'; last connection 'deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file'; SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT and wal_autocheckpoint named.

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints and sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() are always PASSIVE. They run in the thread that did the triggering COMMIT. FULL

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint can run alongside readers but must stop at any WAL frame past a current reader's end mark; it records its progress
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 2.2: 'must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader ... remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got'; 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress'.
